Chapter 4: Addressing Barriers to Intimacy with God
Even when we really want to grow closer to God, it’s pretty common to run into some roadblocks along the way. Maybe you’ve felt it too—distractions, doubts, feeling unworthy, or just plain disappointment from the past. Sound familiar? The truth is, spotting these challenges and gently working through them is a crucial part of your spiritual journey.
One of the biggest hurdles is believing that God is far away, or maybe just too busy for the little things in your day-to-day life. Sometimes, this idea comes from old experiences or messages we’ve picked up—like God is distant, or always demanding more. But what if you could see God more as a loving companion, someone who genuinely cares and enjoys honest conversations with you?
Another barrier a lot of us face is only reaching out to God when things get tough or we need help. It’s totally normal to turn to God in a crisis, but if that’s the only time we connect, it can create distance. Building the habit of talking with God throughout the ordinary moments—the good, the boring, and everything in between—really helps build closeness and trust.
Distractions are probably the most common challenge. You sit down to pray or reflect, and suddenly your mind’s off in a hundred directions. Instead of getting frustrated or feeling guilty, what if you brought those distractions right into your conversation with God? Share your worries, your plans, even those random thoughts. You might be surprised—these moments can actually deepen your connection.
Another thing that can get in the way is feeling like you’re just not “spiritual enough” to approach God. Maybe you’re carrying around a sense of shame, or you worry you don’t measure up. But here’s something important to remember: God isn’t looking for perfection. He welcomes honesty and vulnerability. Bringing your struggles, doubts, and even your failures into your relationship opens the door to deeper trust and real healing.
So, how can you work through these barriers? Here are a few practical tips:
First, when distractions or struggles show up, don’t ignore them. Name them, and invite God right into the middle of what’s happening.
Second, remind yourself often: God’s love for you doesn’t depend on what you achieve or how well you perform.
And third, practice being gentle with yourself. Spiritual growth isn’t a race—it’s something that unfolds over time.
Community matters here, too. Sharing your experiences, your struggles, and your insights with others who are on the same path brings encouragement and fresh perspective. Just knowing you’re not alone can make a world of difference.
In the end, working through these barriers isn’t about erasing every difficulty. It’s about learning to move through them with honesty and grace. Every obstacle can become a chance to build trust, grow in self-awareness, and experience God’s presence in new, meaningful ways.
